A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiCRo research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-learning experiments on HelpSteer2 and RPR, RewardBench results, and ablations of mixture size and contextual-labeling budget.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds an attribute-specific budget study and evaluations using an 8B backbone.

M1.justification: The mixture objectives and Hedge-router Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Optional head handling changes from pruning correlated heads in v1 Appendix C.1 to merging them in v2 Appendix C.3; Section 8 also proposes safety-based masking. These are limited procedural proposals, without evidence that they were incorporated into the reported experiments.

E1.justification: The established dataset coverage is retained. However, the new 8B evaluation names 'HelpSteer' in Appendix C.5 and Table 12, while the main setup specifies HelpSteer2. Both versions also use 'HelpSteer' as shorthand in Figure 4. The PDFs do not resolve whether the new table uses a distinct dataset or the existing one.

E2.justification: The added 8B comparisons in Tables 11–12 use Single Head, Static Mixture, and ARMO, a reduced comparator set relative to the main 3B comparisons, which also include Shared-Base and HyRe variants. Existing comparisons remain unchanged, and no new baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds GRM-Llama3-8B evaluations alongside the original GRM-Llama3.2-3B experiments, reporting Stage-1 heads and routing with 50 samples per attribute. The original experimental settings and implementation parameters are retained; the larger backbone is an additional configuration.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a focused budget study for Creativity, Storytelling, and Linguistic Creativity at 50, 100, and 150 samples per attribute. Appendix C.5 adds a backbone-scalability check. The existing mixture-size and aggregate budget analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 already reports standard-deviation bands over five independent runs in Figure 4. v2 Table 9 additionally supplies attribute-level uncertainty, including for the existing 50-sample setting. Tables 11–12 specify five runs with randomly sampled training examples; no increase in the retained experiments' run counts is stated.

E6.justification: The existing numerical tables and plotted results are retained. New results include Linguistic Creativity accuracy of 0.8808±0.0198 at budget 150 in Table 9, and 8B average accuracies of 0.8438±0.0077 on RPR and 0.7555±0.0027 in the HelpSteer-labeled evaluation. These are additional results under specified conditions, not updates demonstrating same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Theorem 3.2, and its Appendix A proof are unchanged. The mixture definitions, training objectives, and Hedge-update derivation also retain the same mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-BT-model limitations, learning diverse reward heads from binary preferences, and sample-efficient contextual routing. The additional experiments support this existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 changes the explanation for weak attribute performance from noisy contextual signals to limited supervision and possible train–test mismatch. The expanded ethics discussion proposes benchmark auditing, head masking, and human inspection, including an untested assertion that these safeguards preserve performance. Existing limitations concerning implicit user context remain.

D1.justification: The advertised code repository changes from MaxwellJryao/MiCRo in v1 Appendix B to uiuctml/MiCRo on v2's first page. The new scalability experiment identifies GRM-Llama3-8B explicitly. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained in the relocated implementation section.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion, and Table 1 retain the same cited works and research positioning. The added backbone and safety discussions reuse existing references.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely unchanged, with localized revisions to results interpretation and ethics. Appendices B–E are reorganized into experimental details and additional-results subsections, and author affiliation, contact, and acknowledgment text is updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9, 11, and 12, renumbers the existing RewardBench table to Table 10, and rearranges tables, figures, and captions. Table 4 headers are shortened and Figure 1 is resized; the existing result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The targeted budget study and additional 8B evaluations provide useful evidence about attribute-specific weaknesses and performance across backbones. Attribute-level uncertainty makes these findings easier to assess. The gains are limited: the core evidence remains unchanged, the new HelpSteer dataset naming is ambiguous, and the proposed safety safeguards are not experimentally validated.
